results.summary_before: This is a minimal perceptron-based branch predictor that reads branch instruction addresses and ground truth directions via SPI and outputs predictions. It is based on a research paper and uses latch-based memory, with a functional simulation in C++ and CocoTB tests. It requires external hardware to drive inputs and read outputs, and is notable for its use of a perceptron model and detailed debugging features.

The documentation is very thin and does not describe the processor architecture or instruction set. UART communication is emulated within the testbench, and no external hardware is required.

results.notes: Proposed tags and summary described an unrelated siren/light-pattern design.
results.summary_before: This design produces siren-like tones and light patterns reminiscent of 1970s effects, using a chain of D flip-flops to divide the clock into various frequencies. Higher frequencies generate tones for audio output, while lower frequencies control the patterns on a seven-segment display and modulate the tones. A pattern select input chooses between two groups of patterns. External hardware such as a speaker with a series resistor or an audio amplifier is required for sound output.
results.summary: This design is a phase/frequency detector that detects phase shifts between two square waves. It is one of the blocks of a phase locked loop, with a reference clock and feedback clock as inputs and up and inverted down outputs indicating the phase difference. If the feedback clock leads the reference, the up signal shows the difference; if it lags, the down signal shows it. External hardware such as signal generators for square wave inputs is required.

results.summary_before: Convertidor de Tiempo a Digital (TDC) is a time-to-digital converter that measures the width of an input pulse and transmits the digital value via RS232. It includes a counter, a state machine, and an RS232 transmitter operating at 9600 baud with odd parity. The design is intended for interfacing with time-output sensors and was tested in simulation and on an FPGA development board.
results.summary: This is an NCL LFSR, a trivial example to try out self-timed logic. Logic is dual redundantly encoded to distinguish data (DATAx) from no data (NULL). It cannot really be tested without a scope and a way to drive inputs. Silicon test reports are partial: the single C-gate works as expected, but the oscillator goes to a constant value when init is asserted.

results.notes: Proposed tags and summary described an unrelated SPI/I2C register bank.
results.summary_before: This design implements a register bank that can be accessed through either an SPI or an I2C serial interface, with a digital input selecting which interface is active. It is used by writing and reading registers over the selected bus, and the first register is documented as controlling LEDs on the demo board. External hardware may include 2k2 pull-up resistors on the I2C SDA and SCL lines, and testers have used a Bus Pirate and a Pico with internal pull-ups to exercise both interfaces. Silicon tests confirmed read and write access over SPI and I2C, including multi-byte transfers and cross-interface access to the same registers.
results.summary: This design implements a configurable ring oscillator built from manually instantiated gf180mcuD inverter cells, with selectable tap points to set the oscillation frequency. The selected clock drives a worker counter that counts up to 3000, and a VGA sync generator displays the upper bits of the counter as vertical coloured bars. It requires a Tiny VGA PMOD and a VGA monitor, and the ring oscillator output can be measured on uio_out[7:4]. Silicon tests confirmed working VGA output and a ring oscillator frequency of about 78 MHz.

results.summary: This design counts until the heat death of the universe and broadcasts the counter value every second over Ethernet. It re-uses the Teapot Ethernet accelerator wrapper for 100Mbps Ethernet communication in full-duplex mode using a CAT-3/5 cable. The ASIC autonomously sends an application packet with ethtype 0x88b5 every second. It requires an Ethernet 100BASE-T Pmod connector featuring a LAN8720A PHY and a 50MHz oscillator.
